summary: Commerce sits on just 6.5 square miles of flat, industrially zoned Los Angeles Basin land, yet its daytime population dwarfs its roughly 12,200 residents — the Citadel Outlets mall and a massive concentration of warehouses, distribution centers, and manufacturing facilities along the I-5, I-710, and Washington Boulevard corridors make it one of Southern California's densest logistics hubs per capita. That employment base means property tax and sales tax revenue flow generously relative to the small residential footprint, which historically funded a city-owned casino and unusually robust municipal services for a city this size. The tradeoff is tangible: the landscape is dominated by big-box industrial parcels, freight truck traffic, and freeway interchanges rather than tree-lined residential streets, giving the city a fragmented feel where homes cluster in pockets between commercial and industrial stretches. A median home price around $583,200 against a median household income near $71,800 yields a price-to-income ratio above 8:1, making ownership a steep climb even with median rents holding at a relatively moderate $1,420. Property crime rates are strikingly elevated — particularly motor vehicle theft and larceny — likely inflated by the sheer volume of commercial activity and vehicle traffic passing through daily. With 77°F average highs, reliable sunshine, and proximity to both downtown LA and the San Gabriel Valley, Commerce functions less as a destination and more as a workhorse node in the regional economy that happens to have neighborhoods tucked between the gears.
